target_claim.plain: Stable closure is better explained by non-canceling phase-lagged relational recurrence than by node count, triadic topology, or generic attractor dynamics.

null_hypothesis.formal: S_closure is independent of Δφ_R once topology, density, and update strength are controlled.
null_hypothesis.plain: Phase lag is descriptive only; closure is caused by ordinary attractor dynamics.

ablations.change: Randomize Δφ_R each recurrence while preserving lag magnitude distribution
Force phase relation into known cancellation bands
Keep phase lag but remove residue dependence across recurrences
Preserve topology and node count but scramble phase residue
Preserve interaction density and coupling strength but remove coherent phase lag
Use triadic topology with no non-canceling phase residue
ablations.kills_if: Triads match or outperform phase-lag dyads

ablations.change: Use standard attractor update with matched persistence but no phase-lag semantics
ablations.kills_if: Generic attractor matches identity and recurrence metrics

observables.R_phase: correlation between prior phase residue and next recurrence
observables.I_recur: identity-like recurrence under changing local realization
observables.A_return: fraction of recurrences satisfying admissible return

hard_fail_conditions: M8_GENERIC_ATTRACTOR matches M0 on all observables

success_condition_for_hypothesis.plain: Phase-lagged residue must explain closure better than topology, density, node count, random lag, or generic attractors.
